title: Choosing the Candidate Cushion Item When Several Appear — PAP Supply Replenishment Program
content:
**Rule.** When the interface style in use is read from an enrollment's lines in the PAP Supply Replenishment Program, the candidate cushion item is chosen as follows:

1. when two or more cushion items have counted lines in the span, the item with the most counted lines is the candidate, and a tie goes to the item whose newest counted line is newer;
2. when the counted lines in the span are all of one cushion item, that item is the candidate;
3. otherwise the cushion item of the newest counted line is the candidate — where the span holds no counted cushion line, there is no candidate.

The cushion items are the full face mask cushion (A7031), the nasal mask cushion (A7032) and the nasal pillows pair (A7033). Counted lines are lines, not units.

## Input — judgement — output

| Counted cushion lines in the span | Candidate |
|---|---|
| A7032: 3 lines (newest 2 May); A7033: 2 lines (newest 15 May) | A7032 — most lines |
| A7031: 2 lines (newest 10 May); A7033: 2 lines (newest 12 May) | A7033 — tie on lines, newer newest line |
| A7033: 4 lines | A7033 — all of one item |
| none | no candidate |

(All dates hypothetical.)

## Points of judgement

- With two or more items present, the newest line alone does not decide; the count of lines does, and the newest line only breaks a tie.
- Only counted lines in the span take part.
